title: Matrix as Function: T(v) = Av
topic: A matrix-vector multiplication is a linear transformation. The 2×2 matrix A turns the column vector v into Av by taking row-times-column dot products. T(v) = Av is the whole story.

beats.narration: What does a matrix actually do to a vector? Let's compute.

elements.content: A is a rule. v is the input. Av is the output.

beats.narration: Send in a vector. The matrix is the rule. The output is another vector — same dimension, new direction.

elements.content: Left mini-grid with input v = (1, 2) violet
Centre 'machine' — bracketed 2×2 matrix A = [[1, 2],[3, -1]] in chalk
'input → matrix → output' caption strip beneath the three panels

beats.narration: Multiply row by column. One times one plus two times two gives five. Three times one minus one times two gives one. So A v equals the column five, one.

elements.content: Top row of A glows; v column glows; an arrow swings from row · column to first entry of output, animating the dot product
Bottom row of A glows; second entry computed
Output vector (5, 1) appears amber on the right mini-grid

beats.narration: That's it. Every linear function from the plane to the plane is just multiplication by some matrix, written T of v equals A v.

elements.content: Large serif italic equation 'T(v) = A v' centred, with A in chalk, v in violet, A v in amber-300

beats.narration: Pick a matrix. Pick a vector. Multiply. Get a new vector.

elements.content: 'Linear is matrix.' huge serif italic, 'matrix' in amber-300
'Row by column. That is the whole arithmetic.' subtitle
